name: Chicken Chettinad
cuisine: Tamil Nadu (Chettinad / Karaikudi region; South Indian)

ingredients.name: Dry red chillies (sookhi lal mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2–3 chillies (use Kashmiri for colour, Guntur for heat)

ingredients.name: Gingelly oil / sesame oil (til ka tel; untoasted Indian kind)

equipment: Heavy kadai or deep pan with a lid (20 cm), for the curry
Small pan or tawa, for dry-roasting the spices
Mixer-grinder with a small (chutney) jar, for the masala paste
Mixing bowl, small plate (for cooling the spices), knife, chopping board, spatula, measuring spoons
Optional: pressure cooker (cook the chicken 1 whistle instead of simmering, if the pieces are large or from an older bird)

steps.title: Wash the chicken
steps.text: Rinse 200 g chicken pieces under running water and drain well.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, knife and board with soap after handling raw chicken.
steps.visualCue: Water runs clear; no blood pooling
steps.cameraCheck: The drained chicken in a colander
steps.videoShot: Chicken pieces rinsed under a tap.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the chicken with 0.5 g (a pinch) turmeric and 1 g (scant ¼ tsp) salt. Set aside.
steps.visualCue: Every piece evenly yellow
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Hands turning chicken in yellow turmeric.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 70 g onion.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces about 3–4 mm
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped onion
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping onion finely.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 70 g tomato and slit the green chilli.
steps.visualCue: Small, juicy tomato pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato and the slit chilli
steps.videoShot: A knife dicing tomato.

steps.title: Heat the roasting pan
steps.text: Heat a small pan or tawa on low-medium heat, dry (no oil).
steps.visualCue: A drop of water sizzles away in 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: The empty pan on the flame
steps.videoShot: A water drop dancing on the hot pan.

steps.title: Roast the whole spices
steps.text: Add 4 g coriander seeds, 2 g peppercorns, the dry red chillies, 1 g fennel, 1 g cumin, 2 cloves, the cinnamon, 1 cardamom, 1 star-anise petal and the kalpasi (if using). Stir continuously.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low and keep stirring; burnt spices make the curry bitter. If any turn black, start again.
steps.visualCue: Coriander turns a shade darker, the chillies puff and crisp; a strong roasted, peppery smell
steps.cameraCheck: The roasted spices in the pan
steps.videoShot: Spices tumbling and darkening in a dry pan.

steps.title: Roast the poppy seeds
steps.text: Add 2 g poppy seeds and stir.
steps.visualCue: The seeds turn from white to light cream and start to pop
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the poppy seeds in
steps.videoShot: Tiny seeds jumping in the pan.

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: Add 20 g grated coconut and keep stirring.
steps.visualCue: The coconut turns golden-brown and smells toasty, not burnt
steps.cameraCheck: The golden coconut and spices
steps.videoShot: White coconut shreds browning among the spices.

steps.title: Cool the masala
steps.text: Tip everything onto a plate to stop the cooking.
steps.visualCue: Cool enough to touch
steps.cameraCheck: The spread-out masala on the plate
steps.videoShot: Roasted masala tipped onto a steel plate.

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Grind the cooled mix to a powder first, then add 30 ml (2 tbsp) water and grind to a smooth, thick paste.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, dark brown paste with no whole peppercorns
steps.cameraCheck: The paste in the mixer jar
steps.videoShot: The open jar with a thick brown paste.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat 12 ml (2½ tsp) gingelly oil in the kadai on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers
steps.cameraCheck: The oil in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the kadai.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp fennel seeds and the curry leaves.
steps.tip: Stand back; wet curry leaves spit.
steps.visualCue: Fennel darkens slightly; curry leaves crackle and turn glossy
steps.cameraCheck: The tempering in the oil
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves spluttering in hot oil.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and green chilli and fry, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Onion soft and light golden-brown at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The browned onion
steps.videoShot: Onion turning golden in the kadai.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 10 g (2 tsp) ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell is gone
steps.cameraCheck: The onion with the paste mixed in
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring paste into onions.

steps.title: Add the tomato
steps.text: Add the tomato and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt; cook, stirring.
steps.visualCue: The tomato breaks down to a soft, mushy masala
steps.cameraCheck: The softened tomato masala
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing soft tomato.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: The chicken turns opaque white on all sides
steps.cameraCheck: The chicken in the masala
steps.videoShot: Chicken pieces turning white in the masala.

steps.title: Add the ground masala
steps.text: Add all the Chettinad paste (rinse the jar with 2 tbsp of the 120 ml water and add that too). Stir to coat the chicken.
steps.visualCue: The chicken is coated in a thick, dark brown masala
steps.cameraCheck: The coated chicken
steps.videoShot: Brown paste being stirred through the chicken.

steps.title: Add water and simmer
steps.text: Add the rest of the 120 ml water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low heat, stirring every 5 min.
steps.visualCue: The chicken is cooked through; a piece cut at the thickest part shows no pink and clear juices
steps.cameraCheck: A piece of chicken cut open on a spoon
steps.videoShot: The lid lifted on a bubbling brown gravy.

steps.title: Finish the gravy
steps.text: Uncover and cook until the gravy is as thick as you like.
steps.visualCue: A thick, coating gravy with a thin layer of red-brown oil at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The gravy with oil at the edges
steps.videoShot: The spatula dragging through thick gravy.

steps.title: Taste and garnish
steps.text: Taste for salt and pepper, turn off the heat and scatter 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Green coriander on dark brown gravy
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Coriander falling onto the curry.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave covered for 5 min so the spices settle, then serve hot.
steps.tip: The curry tastes even better after a few hours.
steps.visualCue: The gravy thickens a little more
steps.cameraCheck: The served bowl with chicken pieces visible
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from a bowl of Chicken Chettinad.

reasons: lean skinless chicken gives 36 g of protein for about 460 kcal, the gravy is built on whole spices, onion and tomato (8 g fibre), and nothing is deep-fried; 12 ml oil is moderate. Points come off for saturated fat from coconut (about 9 g), sodium (about 1,100 mg) and few vegetables. Restaurant versions usually use more oil (often groundnut or refined oil, sometimes a layer floating on top), more salt and sometimes coconut milk or cream.

researchRating.basis: a classic and widely loved Tamil curry with its own Wikipedia article, on South Indian and North Indian restaurant menus across India and abroad (UK, US, Canada, Singapore and Dubai listings seen), and highly rated on recipe sites: Indian Healthy Recipes 4.97/5 (227 votes), Glebe Kitchen 4.88/5 (32 votes), Yummy Tummy Aarthi 4.07/5 (16 votes). Deduction: Hari Ghotra's version sits at 3.5/5 (447 votes), and the heat and long spice list put some cooks off; restaurant versions are often said to be "Chettinad" in name only.

storage: Cool within 1 hour, then refrigerate in a closed box for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month (the coconut gravy freezes well). Reheat once, in a pan on low heat with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, for 5–6 min until steaming hot right through (or covered in a microwave for 2–3 min, stirring halfway). Thaw frozen curry in the fridge overnight first.
leftoverRemix: Chettinad chicken kothu-style wrap. Pull the chicken off the bone, cook it down with the leftover gravy until almost dry, add a handful of sliced onion and capsicum, and roll it in a warm roti or parotta with a smear of mint chutney. Use within the same 2-day window.
burnOff: about 6.6 km of running (460 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 9.2 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 50 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). Rice or parotta on the side is extra.

navratri.reason: contains chicken, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided under the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains chicken, onion and garlic, avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set.

jain.reason: contains chicken, plus onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

ramadan.reason: use halal chicken. A good iftar main with rice or parotta; at about 1,100 mg sodium (est.) and very peppery-hot it is salty and spicy for sehri unless the salt and chilli are cut.

jain.reason: contains chicken, plus onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots).

glutenFree.reason: chicken, coconut, vegetables and whole spices; this recipe uses no hing (compounded hing contains wheat) and no flour. Check any packaged Chettinad masala label.

dairyFree.reason: no curd, cream, ghee or milk; the richness comes from coconut and gingelly oil.

variants.reason: the Jain diet excludes chicken, and the gravy relies on onion, garlic and fresh ginger (roots). A root-free vegetable Chettinad would be a separate dish.
main recipe already gluten-free (no hing, no flour). Check any packaged masala label.
main recipe already dairy-free (coconut and gingelly oil, no curd, cream or ghee).
